newsitem.title: CANADA: No deal between CAW, Canadian after meeting.
newsitem.headline: No deal between CAW, Canadian after meeting.

text.p: A meeting on Wednesday among Canadian Auto Workers president Buzz Hargrove, Canadian Airlines Corp chief executive Kevin Benson and Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson ended in about 20 minutes with no deal reached by the three parties.
Hargrove and Benson left the meeting visibly upset.
"I am angry as hell," Hargrove told reporters after explaining that the government refused to provide more cash to help the ailing carrier.
Canadian, which has not posted a yearly profit in about a decade, could cease operations by early next year if it failed to find a way to deal with its C$2.8 billion of debt and lease obligations.
Fort Worth-based AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, has a 33 percent ownership stake and 25 percent voting interest in Canadian Airlines International, the operating unit of Canadian.

On Tuesday, AMR agreed to cut its service fees by C$48 million a year over four years to support Canadian's restructuring. AMR said this support was contingent on all parties, including all the Canadian Airlines unions, supporting the restructuring plan.
Hargrove said he would not allow the 3,700 Canadian employees who are CAW members to vote on the company's restructuring proposal.
Benson said he did not see much point in meeting with the company's creditors if he did not have a restructuring plan supported by all six unions.
"I don't know what I can tell our creditors," Benson told reporters. "What can I tell them? We don't have six unions on board. We don't have a plan."
